items.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I got a call to go conduct a bunch of 16 year old kids for President Clinton.

ctx.x: Tell us about your work so far with the Statesmen. Tell us what it means to be in such an elite group and what that means historically for this music.

Well seeing as I’m the newest and the youngest, first of all I know all these guys for years. So that, you know it’s like, when you know — it’s not like going with a bunch of strangers. It’s like a comfortable shoe. And we all know the same people, we all know the same tunes, it’s an honor to be in that company. So in fact I told Buster, I added up when I got the call for this job, I added up the ages of everybody including myself and divided it by seven, and the average age in this band is 79. Now that’s kind…
